text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - On Monday Slovakia begins presenting its side at the International Court of Justice in the Hague in a law suit with Hungary over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the river Danube.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), said it supported Slovakia's membership in NATO, but that it will leave it up to the people to decide how to vote on deployment of foreign military forces and nuclear weapons on Slovak territory, two of the three questions of the forthcoming NATO referendum.
- The ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, at the weekend re-elected its Chairman Jan Luptak to the post.

- Luptak said his party will remain in the ruling coalition until the next election, scheduled for 1998. The ZRS said it was against Slovakia's integration into "western, exploitative" organisations, including NATO.

- The government, in reaction to the opposition-initiated referendum on direct presidential elections, asked the constitutional court to explain whether the constitution can be changed by a referendum.
- The opposition Democratic Union (DU) has elected former foreign minister Eduard Kukan as its a new chairman.
- Eurotel a.s., a U.S.-Slovak joint-venture GSM operator, has signed a roaming agreement with the British GSM operator Cellnet.
SME - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the state-owned monopoly gas distributor SPP and Russia's Gazprom could create a joint-venture to manage transportation of Russian gas.
- Kozlik said that Russian gas was still the most favourable option price-wise, for Slovakia to cover domestic consumption.
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is scheduled to visit Slovakia next April.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Leasing contracts totalled 16.68 billion crowns in 1996, with cars accounting for 58.1 percent, industrial equipment for 25.4 percent and trucks 8.5 percent.
- Some 8,500 new cars were sold in Slovakia in the first two months of the year, with the Czech car maker Skoda accounting for 38 percent of the market.

PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Sunday began a five-day visit to Japan where he is scheduled to meet his Japanese counterpart Ryutaro Hashimoto and Emperor Akihito. - The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying Slovakia's largest confectioner, Jacobs Figaro a.s., will post a pre-tax profit of 60-70 million crowns in 1996, the first profit since Jacobs Suchard took a majority stake in Figaro in 1992. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
